findings.title: A timed-out attempt is abandoned, not stopped: thread, connection and tokens leak
findings.why: When the deadline expires, `_within_deadline` only sets `cancelled` and raises; the worker thread is never joined, never logged, and its late result or exception is dropped into `outcome` and lost. The abandoned call is still inside the model's `_stream`, and `until_cancelled` only looks at `cancelled` after the next chunk arrives, so it can keep streaming and calling `run_manager.on_llm_new_token` for up to `idle_seconds` (300 s by default) while the caller has already moved on to the next turn/retry. Consequences: (a) tokens generated by the abandoned attempt are never reported through `on_llm_end`, so the token budget under-counts and can be overrun; (b) two live attempts share the same `run_manager` and HTTP client, so callbacks from the dead attempt interleave with the new run's; (c) an exception raised in the abandoned thread (including `BudgetExceededError`) vanishes silently; (d) each timed-out attempt permanently holds a connection/thread for the whole idle window.

findings.title: A reply cut off mid-stream is accepted as complete because only empty replies are checked
findings.why: With streaming (now the default) a cleanly closed SSE stream that never carried a finish chunk does not raise: the merged `ChatResult` simply has `generation_info["finish_reason"]` (and `response_metadata`) None plus whatever partial content arrived. `_check_not_empty` only rejects replies with no content and no tool calls, so a half-finished tool call or half-finished JSON answer passes the check and is returned as a complete reply. The change promises that broken connections are retried, but the retry only fires for exceptions, and the code already knows `finish is None` can mean 'did not finish' (it uses it for the empty case) — it just never applies that to non-empty replies.

findings.title: A 200 response whose stream carries no chunks is not treated as an empty reply
findings.why: `generate_from_stream` cannot return an empty result: when the iterator yields nothing (service closes the stream with no SSE data, e.g. an overloaded OpenAI-compatible server) it raises `ValueError`/`AssertionError`. `retry_wait` returns None for anything that is not an `APIStatusError`, `APIConnectionError`, transport error or `EmptyReplyError`, so this 'empty reply with no finish reason' fails the call immediately instead of being retried, contrary to decision D-030. `_check_not_empty` is never reached because the failure happens one line earlier.

findings.title: With streaming off, the two-minute whole-reply bound is only a per-read timeout
findings.why: `WHOLE_REPLY_SECONDS` is passed as httpx's `read` timeout, which is reset by every successful socket read, and the actual deadline is `clock() + time_left`, which is the remaining review time (or `math.inf` for the summarizer model built with `model_for(math.inf)`). A service that keeps trickling body bytes can therefore take far longer than two minutes, and with an infinite deadline nothing else bounds the call, so the rule stated in D-029 ('a whole reply must arrive within two minutes') is not actually enforced.
